overview: Herrerasaurus was one of the largest predators of the Ischigualasto fauna, reaching six metres long around 231 million years ago. Its flexible intramandibular joint — a sliding articulation between the dentary and postdentary bones unique among early dinosaurs — allowed a powerful grip on struggling prey.

Its phylogenetic position remains debated: most analyses treat it as either a basal saurischian (Herrerasauridae) or an early theropod. Either way it documents the very rapid ecological diversification of early dinosaurs in the Late Triassic of South America.

articles.title: Discovery and systematic controversy
articles.body: Reig named the species in 1963 from fragments; a near-complete skeleton found in 1988 by Sereno and Novas transformed understanding. The intramandibular joint is its most distinctive anatomical feature. Whether Herrerasaurus sits within Theropoda or as a more basal saurischian is one of the most actively debated questions in early dinosaur phylogenetics.

articles.title: Anatomy
articles.body: Despite its size, Herrerasaurus retained five digits on the hand (two vestigial) and relatively short arms. The pelvis already shows the perforate acetabulum diagnostic of all dinosaurs. Powerful hindlimbs confirm full bipedality from the outset of its existence.

articles.title: Triassic context
articles.body: At 231 Ma, dinosaurs were not yet dominant: rhynchosaurs, cynodonts and rauisuchians (such as Saurosuchus) were more abundant. Herrerasaurus was the apex dinosaurian predator in an ecosystem still dominated by non-dinosaurian archosaurs, making it a key taxon for understanding predator-prey dynamics at the origin of the dinosaur radiation.

record.mya: late Carnian, approximately 231-229 million years ago
record.description: Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis was an early predatory dinosaur from the Ischigualasto Formation of Argentina. Multiple skeletons, including complete skulls and very substantial postcrania, document a lightly built biped; whether herrerasaurids lie inside Theropoda or just outside the sauropodomorph-theropod split remains debated.
facts: Ischisaurus cattoi and Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis are generally regarded as synonyms of Herrerasaurus.
Recurved serrated teeth and grasping hands support carnivory.
Its mixture of primitive and derived features makes root-level classification unstable.

review.ageReviewNote: The principal Ischigualasto occurrences are radiometrically constrained near 231-229 Ma.
